nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a topological space equipped with an atlas of charts modelled on $\mathbb{R}^3$, so that $M$ is locally homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$. Then $M$ is a topological 3-manifold if and only if $M$ is Hausdorff and second-countable.
nodes.title: Characterization of topological 3-manifolds

nodes.summary: A topological 3-manifold with boundary: a Hausdorff, second-countable topological space locally homeomorphic to the Euclidean half-space `EuclideanHalfSpace 2`.
nodes.title: Topological 3-manifold with boundary

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a topological space equipped with an atlas of charts, each a homeomorphism from an open subset of $M$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$, whose domains cover $M$. Then $M$ is a topological 3-manifold if it is Hausdorff and second-countable.
nodes.title: Topological 3-manifold

nodes.summary: Every topological 3-manifold $M$ is locally compact, since $\mathbb{R}^3$ is.
nodes.title: Topological 3-manifolds are locally compact
